text.p: Virginia projects a surplus of $220 million for the 1996-1998 budget cycle, the Norfolk Daily Press reported Friday.

Updated forecasts provided Thursday to the General Assembly's Senate Finance Committee predict the state will take in about $167 million more than initially projected in tax revenues this year. Combined with surplus savings, new money available for the General Assembly to allocate in January could exceed $220 million.
After accounting for new costs such as prisons, schools and mandated services, that would still leave $115 million of new revenue for allocation by the General Assembly.
Lawmakers said the money represents a small part of Virginia's two-year, $34 billion budget, but signals that the state's recent fiscal pressure may be easing.
Virginia was forced to cut more than $2 billion from its budget after weathering a recession in 1991.
"For the first time in years, I think we can see clear signs of a stable fiscal picture ahead," Sen. John Chichester, R-Stafford, told the newspaper.
